attribution_limitations: Table 1 holds 38 rows (37 literature cases plus the authors' own case) but no row is labelled as the index case. The last row (sex, age, time after colonoscopy, treatment and condition) agrees with the case text, but the table does not state that this row is the index patient.

Source conflict about symptoms before the colonoscopy: the Discussion says there were no symptoms prior to the procedure, while the abstract says the colonoscopy was done during the investigation of nontypical abdominal pain and the case text describes abdominal pain at admission and pain that reoccurred after the colonoscopy.

The general practitioners considered rehydration and empirical antibiotic administration necessary as initial treatment; the text does not separately state that either was given, which antibiotic was meant, or when.
Early appendicitis is described as most probably excluded from the differential diagnosis because colonoscopy findings from the appendix were normal; this is a hedged exclusion.

The authors support a fecalith, possibly introduced by air insufflation, as the causal event, but state that a fecalith already present before the colonoscopy and perforation due to overinsufflation or scope trauma could not be excluded; they also call the intraoperative condition a postcolonoscopy complication and say peritonitis could be explained by the 20-hour interval from mild postcolonoscopy symptoms to surgical management.

The severe symptoms and the mild postcolonoscopy symptoms used for the six-hour and 20-hour intervals are not explicitly identified with the acute abdomen presentation or the recurrent abdominal pain.

The Figure 5 caption lists a fecalith and the Discussion lists impacted stool in the appendix found after the open appendectomy; the text does not state they are the same finding. The caption also names the intraoperative finding acute appendicitis with peritonitis while the case text says perforated appendicitis with peritonitis.
The WBC and neutrophil values in the acute abdomen sentence have no stated sampling time, and only the white blood cell count is classified (without white blood cell count disturbance).
Colonoscopy findings from the appendix are called normal in the Discussion while the case text gives the examined extent as up to 10 cm proximally to the ileocecal valve.
